questions.question_text: An oil slick spreads in a circle whose radius increases at $0.5$ m/min. At what rate is the area of the slick increasing when the radius is $20$ m?

options.why: Stopped at $\dfrac{dA}{dr} = 2\pi r$ and never multiplied by the given rate $0.5$ m/min.
Substituted $r = 20$ into $A = \pi r^{2}$ first and multiplied that area by $0.5$, instead of differentiating first.
Differentiated $\pi r^{2}$ as $\pi r$, losing the factor of $2$.

questions.solution_text:
$\dfrac{dr}{dt} = 0.5$ m/min and $\dfrac{dA}{dt}$ is wanted.
$A = \pi r^{2}$
$\dfrac{dA}{dr} = 2\pi r$
$\dfrac{dA}{dt} = 2\pi r \times 0.5$
$= \pi r$
When $r = 20$:
$\dfrac{dA}{dt} = 20\pi$ m²/min

questions.question_text: A spherical hailstone melts so that its radius decreases at $0.4$ mm/min. At what rate is its volume changing when the radius is $5$ mm?

options.why: Used $\dfrac{dr}{dt} = 0.4$ instead of $-0.4$, ignoring that the hailstone is shrinking.
Stopped at $\dfrac{dV}{dr} = 4\pi r^{2}$ and never multiplied by the given rate.
Never multiplied by the given rate and also treated the shrinking radius as a positive rate.

questions.solution_text:
The radius is decreasing, so $\dfrac{dr}{dt} = -0.4$ mm/min.
$V = \dfrac{4}{3}\pi r^{3}$
$\dfrac{dV}{dr} = 4\pi r^{2}$
$\dfrac{dV}{dt} = 4\pi r^{2} \times (-0.4)$
$= -1.6\pi r^{2}$
When $r = 5$:
$\dfrac{dV}{dt} = -1.6\pi (25)$
$= -40\pi$ mm³/min

questions.question_text: A cube-shaped block of stone is eroded so that each edge shortens at $0.03$ cm/s, and the block stays a cube. At what rate is its total surface area changing when each edge is $20$ cm?

options.why: Used $\dfrac{dx}{dt} = 0.03$ instead of $-0.03$, ignoring that the edges are shortening.
Differentiated $S = 6x^{2}$ as $6x$ instead of $12x$.
Differentiated $6x^{2}$ as $6x$ and also dropped the negative sign of the given rate.

questions.solution_text:
The edges are shortening, so $\dfrac{dx}{dt} = -0.03$ cm/s.
$S = 6x^{2}$
$\dfrac{dS}{dx} = 12x$
$\dfrac{dS}{dt} = 12x \times (-0.03)$
$= -0.36x$
When $x = 20$:
$\dfrac{dS}{dt} = -0.36(20)$
$= -7.2$ cm²/s

options.why: Used $\dfrac{dr}{dt} = 0.05$ instead of $-0.05$, ignoring that the radius is being ground away.
Stopped at $\dfrac{dV}{dr} = 80\pi r$ and never multiplied by the given rate.
Never multiplied by the given rate and also dropped its negative sign.

questions.solution_text:
The radius is decreasing, so $\dfrac{dr}{dt} = -0.05$ cm/min.
$V = \pi r^{2}h$ with $h = 40$
$V = 40\pi r^{2}$
$\dfrac{dV}{dr} = 80\pi r$
$\dfrac{dV}{dt} = 80\pi r \times (-0.05)$
$= -4\pi r$
When $r = 12$:
$\dfrac{dV}{dt} = -4\pi (12)$
$= -48\pi$ cm³/min

options.why: Used $\dfrac{dV}{dt} = 3$ instead of $-3$, ignoring that the filter is draining.
Kept the radius fixed at $5$ cm instead of using $r = \dfrac{h}{3}$ to write $V$ in terms of $h$.
Kept the radius fixed at $5$ cm and also dropped the negative sign of the draining rate.

questions.solution_text:
The filter is draining, so $\dfrac{dV}{dt} = -3$ cm³/s.
Similar triangles give $\dfrac{r}{h} = \dfrac{5}{15}$, so $r = \dfrac{h}{3}$.
$V = \dfrac{1}{3}\pi r^{2}h$
$= \dfrac{1}{3}\pi \left(\dfrac{h}{3}\right)^{2}h$
$= \dfrac{\pi h^{3}}{27}$
$\dfrac{dV}{dh} = \dfrac{\pi h^{2}}{9}$
When $h = 6$:
$\dfrac{dV}{dh} = \dfrac{36\pi}{9} = 4\pi$
$-3 = 4\pi \times \dfrac{dh}{dt}$
$\dfrac{dh}{dt} = -\dfrac{3}{4\pi}$ cm/s

options.why: Used $\dfrac{ds}{dy} = \dfrac{s}{y} = \dfrac{100}{80}$, turning the derivative upside down.
Used the horizontal distance over the hypotenuse, $\dfrac{60}{100}$, instead of $\dfrac{y}{s}$.
Assumed the distance from the observer grows at the same rate as the balloon rises.

questions.solution_text:
$\dfrac{dy}{dt} = 3$ m/s and $\dfrac{ds}{dt}$ is wanted.
By Pythagoras, $s = \sqrt{y^{2} + 3600}$.
$\dfrac{ds}{dy} = \dfrac{2y}{2\sqrt{y^{2} + 3600}}$
$= \dfrac{y}{\sqrt{y^{2} + 3600}}$
When $y = 80$:
$\sqrt{6400 + 3600} = 100$
$\dfrac{ds}{dy} = \dfrac{80}{100} = 0.8$
$\dfrac{ds}{dt} = 0.8 \times 3$
$= 2.4$ m/s

options.why: Used $\dfrac{ds}{dx} = \dfrac{2}{5}$, the height ratio itself, instead of solving the similar-triangle equation for $s$.
Used $\dfrac{ds}{dx} = \dfrac{3}{2}$, inverting the fraction obtained from the similar triangles.
Assumed the shadow lengthens at the same rate as the person walks.

questions.solution_text:
Let $x$ be the distance from the post and $s$ the shadow length, so $\dfrac{dx}{dt} = 1.2$ m/s.
Similar triangles give $\dfrac{s}{s + x} = \dfrac{2}{5}$.
$5s = 2s + 2x$
$3s = 2x$
$s = \dfrac{2x}{3}$
$\dfrac{ds}{dx} = \dfrac{2}{3}$
$\dfrac{ds}{dt} = \dfrac{2}{3} \times 1.2$
$= 0.8$ m/s

questions.question_text: A spherical gas storage tank is emptied at $20\pi$ cm³/s. At what rate is the radius of the gas sphere changing at the instant when its volume is $972\pi$ cm³?

options.why: Used $\dfrac{dV}{dt} = 20\pi$ instead of $-20\pi$, ignoring that the tank is emptying.
Divided by $4\pi r^{3}$ instead of by $\dfrac{dV}{dr} = 4\pi r^{2}$.
Divided by $4\pi r^{3}$ and also dropped the negative sign of the emptying rate.

questions.solution_text:
The tank is emptying, so $\dfrac{dV}{dt} = -20\pi$ cm³/s.
First find the radius at that instant.
$\dfrac{4}{3}\pi r^{3} = 972\pi$
$r^{3} = 729$
$r = 9$ cm
$\dfrac{dV}{dr} = 4\pi r^{2}$
$\dfrac{dV}{dt} = 4\pi r^{2} \times \dfrac{dr}{dt}$
When $r = 9$:
$-20\pi = 324\pi \times \dfrac{dr}{dt}$
$\dfrac{dr}{dt} = -\dfrac{20}{324}$
$= -\dfrac{5}{81}$ cm/s

questions.question_text: A spherical bubble of gas in molten glass grows so that its surface area increases at a constant $12$ cm²/s. At what rate is its volume increasing when the radius is $7$ cm?

options.why: Used $\dfrac{dV}{dt} = r \times \dfrac{dS}{dt}$ instead of $\dfrac{r}{2} \times \dfrac{dS}{dt}$.
Stopped after finding $\dfrac{dr}{dt}$ and never went on to the volume.
Assumed the volume grows at the same numerical rate as the surface area.

questions.solution_text:
$\dfrac{dS}{dt} = 12$ cm²/s and $\dfrac{dV}{dt}$ is wanted.
First find $\dfrac{dr}{dt}$.
$S = 4\pi r^{2}$
$\dfrac{dS}{dr} = 8\pi r$
When $r = 7$:
$12 = 8\pi (7) \times \dfrac{dr}{dt}$
$\dfrac{dr}{dt} = \dfrac{12}{56\pi} = \dfrac{3}{14\pi}$ cm/s
Now use the volume.
$V = \dfrac{4}{3}\pi r^{3}$
$\dfrac{dV}{dr} = 4\pi r^{2}$
$\dfrac{dV}{dt} = 4\pi (49) \times \dfrac{3}{14\pi}$
$= \dfrac{588}{14}$
$= 42$ cm³/s
